threads.body:
The `declarative_name` for the URL-template-rules config is `java.common.http.client.url_template_rules/development`, but the agent reads this structured list at the key `url_template_rules` with no `/development` suffix (`RegexUrlTemplateCustomizerInitializer.java:35` calls `.get("http").get("client").getStructuredList("url_template_rules", ...)`, and the integration-test resource `instrumentation-api-incubator/.../declarative-config.yaml` nests it as `url_template_rules:` without the suffix). Per the stability convention (`.github/agents/knowledge/config-property-stability.md`), the `/development` suffix marks a distinct experimental YAML key, so a user following this metadata would place rules under a key the agent never reads. The suffix should be dropped so the documented declarative path matches the key actually consumed.

Note: the same incorrect `java.common.http.client.url_template_rules/development` value was added to every metadata.yaml in this PR that documents this config (e.g. apache-httpclient-*, async-http-client-*, netty-*, okhttp-*, ktor-*, play-ws-*, vertx-http-client-*, jetty-httpclient-*, armeria-1.3, akka-http-10.0, pekko-http-1.0, reactor-netty-1.0, ratpack-1.7, spring-web-6.0, jodd-http-4.2, google-http-client-1.19, http-url-connection, kubernetes-client-7.0, apache-httpasyncclient-4.1), and should be corrected in all of them.

+Some configurations are **lists of objects** in declarative configuration even though their flat
+system-property form is a scalar or map. For these, keep `type` describing the flat form and add:

+- `declarative_schema`: the per-item object schema, mirroring the JSON-schema style used by
+  [opentelemetry-configuration](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-configuration). It

+  `properties`.
+

+```

threads.body: This line lists `integer` as a valid `type` value, but `ConfigurationType` has no `INTEGER` constant — the enum value is `INT` (serialized as `int`), and `ConfigurationType.from("integer")` would throw. Existing metadata files use `type: int` (e.g. `instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/metadata.yaml`). Since this line enumerates the valid flat types, `integer` should be `int`.
